content.title: What is ResultSet?
content.description: ResultSet is a JDBC interface that represents the data returned by a SQL SELECT query. It allows Java applications to retrieve and process rows returned from a database.

content.content: When a SELECT query is executed using JDBC, the database returns the matching records as a ResultSet. The ResultSet object acts like a cursor that points to one row at a time, allowing applications to iterate through records and retrieve column values using various getter methods.

content.title: Why Use ResultSet?
content.content: ResultSet provides an organized way to access database records one row at a time while supporting different data types such as integers, strings, dates, and floating-point numbers.
A ResultSet object is obtained by executing a SELECT query using either Statement or PreparedStatement.

content.title: Creating a ResultSet
content.code:
Statement stmt = con.createStatement();
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM students");

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: The ResultSet cursor starts before the first row. Calling next() moves the cursor to the next available record.

content.content: The next() method moves the cursor to the next row. It returns true if another row exists; otherwise, it returns false.
ResultSet provides various getter methods to retrieve values according to their data types.

content.title: Reading Column Values

content.content: Column values can be accessed either by column name or by column index (starting from 1).

content.title: Column Access Example
content.code:
String name = rs.getString("name");
String city = rs.getString(3);

content.content: Besides next(), scrollable ResultSet objects provide additional cursor movement methods.

content.title: Note
content.content: Methods like previous(), first(), and last() require a scrollable ResultSet. By default, ResultSet objects are forward-only.

rows: Supports scrolling and reflects database changes

content.title: ResultSet Traversal
content.space_complexity: Depends on JDBC driver and fetched data

content.title: Reading a Spreadsheet
content.content: Imagine reading an Excel spreadsheet row by row. You move to each row, read the values from its columns, and continue until all rows have been processed. ResultSet works in the same way.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: ResultSet, cursor movement, next(), getInt(), getString(), ResultSet types, scrollable ResultSet, column indexing, PreparedStatement, and JDBC CRUD operations are commonly asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Why must next() be called before reading data?
items.answer: The cursor initially points before the first row. Calling next() positions it on the first available record.

items.question: Can ResultSet be used after closing the Statement or Connection?
items.answer: No. Closing the associated Statement or Connection usually closes the ResultSet as well.

items.question: Should column indexes always be preferred?
items.answer: No. Accessing columns by name improves readability and maintainability.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: ResultSet stores rows returned by SELECT queries and allows applications to traverse records using a cursor.
